title: Create a data quality check
description:
Add a dbt-test-style assertion to a warehouse table, a saved query (view or materialized view), a data
catalog metric, or a PostHog table (events, persons, groups). Name the subject with subject_type
('table', 'view', 'metric' or 'posthog_table') and subject_uuid, both from data-quality-subjects. A check
passes when it finds zero failing rows.

Query `system.information_schema.data_quality_checks` first — re-creating an identical check is a no-op,
but a near-duplicate with different config is noise for whoever reviews the results.

On a table or a view, prefer a generic type over custom_sql. Config per type:
  - not_null, unique: no config; set column_name.
  - accepted_values: {"values": ["paid", "refunded"]}; set column_name.
  - relationships: {"to_subject_type": "table", "to_subject_uuid": "<uuid>", "to_column": "id"}; set
    column_name. to_subject_type takes 'table', 'view' or 'posthog_table'. Add "to_lookback_hours" to look
    for a match only among the referenced subject's recent rows, which only a target with a time column
    accepts.
  - row_count: {"min": 1} and/or {"max": 1000000}; no column_name.
  - freshness: {"max_age_minutes": 60}; set column_name to a timestamp column.
  - custom_sql: {"query": "select 1 from orders where total < 0"}; every row it returns is a failure.

Add "lookback_hours" to any config to check only the rows from the last N hours, by the subject's own time
column: timestamp on events, created_at on persons and groups. Optional, and only for a subject that has
one -- a warehouse table, a view and a metric do not. Without it the check reads the whole table, which on
events is expensive. custom_sql takes no lookback_hours; put the time filter in the query. Changing the
window creates a new check, so update the existing one to keep its history.

A metric supports custom_sql only, and takes no column_name. Its query must read the {metric} relation
exactly once and cannot use CTEs: {"query": "select * from {metric} where orders < 100"}. Call
data-quality-check-types with the subject_type to see which types that kind of subject supports.

Use severity 'error' when bad data should block trusting the model, 'warn' when it is worth surfacing but
not acting on. A check on a warehouse table runs after each sync of it, a check on a view when the view
refreshes, and a check on a metric or a PostHog table on that subject's schedule.

methodDocumentation.text: Create a check on the table, view or metric named by subject_type and subject_uuid, or refine the one already carrying the same fingerprint. Re-creating a semantically identical check returns 200 and the existing row, never a duplicate.
